body.statement:
Fix \((P,B^0,\varepsilon,\pi_0)\in\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{pub}}\), and let \(\mathcal O_G\) be its observed moments for an arbitrary view graph \(G\). For every \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\), the fiber \(\mathfrak F_G(\mathcal O_G)\) contains a centered jointly Gaussian mechanism whose common order is \(\pi\) and whose coefficient family is \(B_\pi\). Conversely, if \((\widetilde P,\widetilde B,\widetilde\varepsilon,\widetilde\pi)\in\mathfrak F_G(\mathcal O_G)\) and \(\widetilde\pi=\pi\), then \(\widetilde B=B_\pi\). Consequently,
\[
 \Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)=\mathfrak S_V,
 \qquad
 \Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)=\{T_\pi:\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\}.
\]
In the Gaussian witnesses, within-view disturbance coordinates are independent and nondegenerate, while off-diagonal cross-view residual covariances are retained as unrestricted nuisance covariances rather than tested for zero.
body.proof_tex:
Stack the views in a fixed order, write
\(\Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{Cov}_P((X^{(a)})_{a\in M})\), and
fix \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\). The argument in
\(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\), applied within every view, shows
that \(\Sigma^{aa}\succ0\); hence all regressions defining
\(B_\pi^{(a)}\) exist. Put
\[
 \mathcal L_\pi=\operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}(L_\pi^{(a)}),
 \qquad
 S_\pi=\mathcal L_\pi\Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}\mathcal L_\pi^{\mathsf T}.
 \tag{2}
\]
Each \(L_\pi^{(a)}\) is unit lower triangular after reindexing by \(\pi\),
so it is invertible. Since \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}\) is a covariance
matrix, (2) gives \(S_\pi\succeq0\).

We next identify its within-view blocks. Let
\(e_k^{(a)}\) be the residual from regressing
\(X_{\pi(k)}^{(a)}\) on
\((X_{\pi(1)}^{(a)},\ldots,X_{\pi(k-1)}^{(a)})\). The normal equations
give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_P(e_k^{(a)},X_{\pi(\ell)}^{(a)})=0
 \quad(\ell<k).
 \tag{3}
\]
For \(\ell<k\), the earlier residual \(e_\ell^{(a)}\) is a linear
combination of \(X_{\pi(1)}^{(a)},\ldots,X_{\pi(\ell)}^{(a)}\), all of
which lie in the predecessor span in (3). Therefore
\(\operatorname{Cov}_P(e_k^{(a)},e_\ell^{(a)})=0\). Moreover, positive
definiteness of \(\Sigma^{aa}\) implies that the residual variance is the
strictly positive Schur complement
\[
 d_{k,a}=\Sigma^{aa}[\pi(k),\pi(k)]-
 \Sigma^{aa}[\pi(k),A_{k-1}]
 \{\Sigma^{aa}[A_{k-1},A_{k-1}]\}^{-1}
 \Sigma^{aa}[A_{k-1},\pi(k)]>0.
 \tag{4}
\]
Thus every diagonal block \(S_\pi^{aa}=R_\pi^{aa}\) is diagonal with a
strictly positive diagonal.

Choose an orthogonal diagonalization
\(S_\pi=U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{mp})U^{\mathsf T}\),
where \(\lambda_s\ge0\), and set
\(S_\pi^{1/2}=U\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{\lambda_1},\ldots,
\sqrt{\lambda_{mp}})U^{\mathsf T}\). If \(g\) has \(mp\) independent
standard normal coordinates, define
\[
 \widetilde\varepsilon=S_\pi^{1/2}g,
 \qquad
 \widetilde X=\mathcal L_\pi^{-1}\widetilde\varepsilon.
 \tag{5}
\]
Then \(\widetilde\varepsilon\) is centered jointly Gaussian with covariance
\(S_\pi\), and
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde X)
 =\mathcal L_\pi^{-1}S_\pi\mathcal L_\pi^{-\mathsf T}
 =\Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}.
 \tag{6}
\]
For a fixed view \(a\), its disturbance covariance is the positive diagonal
matrix in (3)--(4). Its characteristic function therefore factors as
\[
 \mathbb E\exp\!\left(i\sum_{j\in V}t_j
 \widetilde\varepsilon_j^{(a)}\right)
 =\exp\!\left(-\tfrac12\sum_{j\in V}d_{j,a}t_j^2\right)
 =\prod_{j\in V}\exp(-d_{j,a}t_j^2/2),
\]
which proves that the within-view coordinates are independent, centered,
and nondegenerate. Equation (5) also gives
\(\widetilde X^{(a)}=B_\pi^{(a)}\widetilde X^{(a)}+
\widetilde\varepsilon^{(a)}\), and the coefficient matrices share the order
\(\pi\). Thus the witness belongs to
\(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{pub}}\). By (6), it matches every observed
diagonal block and edge block, so it belongs to
\(\mathfrak F_G(\mathcal O_G)\). This proves existence in the first
direction. Notice that the cross-view blocks of \(S_\pi\) in (2), including
their off-diagonal coordinate entries, were carried into the Gaussian
witness without any zero constraint; they are nuisance covariance.

For the converse, take
\((\widetilde P,\widetilde B,\widetilde\varepsilon,
\widetilde\pi)\in\mathfrak F_G(\mathcal O_G)\) with
\(\widetilde\pi=\pi\). Fix a view \(a\), a position \(k\), set
\(r=\pi(k)\), and let \(A=\{\pi(1),\ldots,\pi(k-1)\}\). The shared-order
condition makes row \(r\) of \(\widetilde B^{(a)}\) zero outside \(A\), so
the structural equation is
\[
 \widetilde X_r^{(a)}=
 \widetilde B^{(a)}[r,A]\widetilde X_A^{(a)}+
 \widetilde\varepsilon_r^{(a)}. \tag{7}
\]
The leading subsystem is triangular and therefore
\[
 \widetilde X_A^{(a)}=
 (I-\widetilde B^{(a)}[A,A])^{-1}widetilde\varepsilon_A^{(a)}.
 \tag{8}
\]
The product disturbance law within view \(a\) makes
\(\widetilde\varepsilon_r^{(a)}\) independent of
\(\widetilde\varepsilon_A^{(a)}\). By (8), it is therefore independent of
\(\widetilde X_A^{(a)}\); centeredness and finite second moments give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_{\widetilde P}
 (\widetilde\varepsilon_r^{(a)},\widetilde X_A^{(a)})=0.
 \tag{9}
\]
Taking covariance of (7) with \(\widetilde X_A^{(a)}\), using (9), and then
using fiber membership to replace the marginal covariance by the observed
one yields
\[
 \Sigma^{aa}[r,A]
 =\widetilde B^{(a)}[r,A]\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]. \tag{10}
\]
The matrix on the right is invertible by the marginal positive-definiteness
proved at the start of this argument, so
\[
 \widetilde B^{(a)}[r,A]
 =\Sigma^{aa}[r,A]\{\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]\}^{-1}
 =B_\pi^{(a)}[r,A]. \tag{11}
\]
Both coefficient rows vanish outside \(A\). Since \(a\) and \(k\) were
arbitrary, \(\widetilde B=B_\pi\). Thus every coefficient in the fiber is
one of the \(T_\pi\), while the first direction realizes every such tuple.
Taking respectively the order and coefficient projections in
\(\texttt{def:compatible-orders}\) and
\(\texttt{def:identified-tuple-set}\) proves
\[
 \Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)=\mathfrak S_V,
 \qquad
 \Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)=\{T_\pi:\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\}.
\]
body.justification: The theorem proves both the explicit Gaussian realization of every order and the normal-equation exhaustiveness of the independently defined published mechanism fiber.
body.gap: The anchor's structural model allows cross-view nuisance dependence, but no supplied result identifies both projections of the complete second-moment compatibility fiber under that unrestricted dependence.
body.consumer: Analysts learn that partial cross-view covariance cannot prune marginal orderwise coefficient tuples without an additional cross-view restriction, while every compatible coefficient family is still enumerated.
